scope: Read-only userspace terminal and display binding, plus later Wayland and Chonkstep sources. Kernel video-console boot-args are Astra's. Framebuffer and IOGOP matching are Claude's. This file does not read raw test 009 and does not boot anything.

booted_userspace.single_user_shell: /bin/sh rewrites argv0 to sh and execs /private/var/select/sh, which this image links to /bin/zsh
booted_userspace.tty_owner: devfs node major 0 is cnopen, which forwards to km_tty[0]

console_binding.single_user: launchctl do_single_user_mode2 opens /dev/console and execl /bin/sh. Source: src/Libraries/XPC/launchctl/launchctl.c.
console_binding.after_single_user_exits_0: org.puredarwin.console-login RunAtLoad starts /usr/libexec/pd-console-login, which also opens /dev/console and execs /bin/zsh -l. Source: pd_console_login.c and org.puredarwin.console-login.plist.
console_binding.etc_ttys: image.nix writes /dev/console /bin/zsh -l. The -s path does not consult it.
console_binding.same_device: Neither login path opens a framebuffer. Both write the kernel km tty.

why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.launcher_bootargs: -v -s debug=0x14e keepsyms=1 serial=3 serial-device-name=uart0 disable-uart-irq=1 cpus=1 rd=md0 serial_video_mirror=1 pdtextboot=1
why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.bootargs_source: integrations/puredarwin/m1-bringup/host_progress.py BOOTARGS. gopconsole is not in that string. This review did not boot it.
why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.hv_set_bootargs_display: sources/m1n1-baseline/proxyclient/m1n1/hv/__init__.py set_bootargs sets video.display=0 when -v is present. configure_display_console then sets video.display=2 after the geometry checks and records physical_panel_observed=false.
why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.arm_pe_create_console: sources/puredarwin-baseline/src/Kernel/xnu/pexpert/arm/pe_init.c: serial=3 has already selected the UART. A nonzero v_display initializes text mode unless display==1, which is graphics mode. switch_to_video_console runs only when serial_video_mirror or gopconsole is also set. v_display 0 does not take that branch, so the active console stays the UART.
why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.pdtextboot: sources/puredarwin-m1-bringup/src/Kernel/xnu/osfmk/console/video_console.c defaults pdtextboot to 1 and, when the boot is text mode, keeps text after IOGraphics takes the console. The helper passes pdtextboot=1. That flag is not a panel observation.
why_the_panel_can_stay_on_an_old_frame.userspace_change_that_does_not_paint_the: Leaving -s so pd-console-login runs still opens /dev/console.

route_to_a_visible_interactive_shell.next_stop: The accepted shell's existing /dev/console bytes painted by the kernel video console onto the firmware framebuffer, then scanned out on the 13-inch panel.
depends_on: Astra: video console actually selected. On this source that is nonzero v_display plus serial_video_mirror or gopconsole. The helper sets display=2 after set_bootargs and passes serial_video_mirror=1.
Claude: a framebuffer whose scanout is the 13-inch panel. Firmware framebuffer bytes, including a later host PNG of a paused capture, are not that proof.
route_to_a_visible_interactive_shell.not_acceptance: A kernel debug frame already on the panel is not a userland shell. A QEMU or Linux shell is not this display. A decoded capture is not physical panel proof.

later_wayland_in_the_pin.arm64_virt_wayland_image: image-arm64-virt-wayland uses imageExtraPackagesArm64Nox, which includes swayArm64NoxBuild and wlrootsArm64NoxBuild, on the virt KC rather than the T8103 bring-up collection
later_wayland_in_the_pin.wlroots_backend: nix/pkgs/wayland/wlroots.nix configures -Dbackends=puredarwin and empty renderers and allocators
later_wayland_in_the_pin.autocreate_gap: wlroots backend.c selects puredarwin only when WLR_BACKENDS names it. With that variable unset, autocreate still attempts a DRM session and fails closed when DRM is compiled out
later_wayland_in_the_pin.framebuffer_client: backend/puredarwin/output.c calls PDGOPOpen. src/Libraries/PDGOP/PDGOP.c matches IOVirtIOGPU, then IOGOPFramebuffer, then IOFramebuffer
later_wayland_in_the_pin.foot: footArm64Build is a Wayland client attribute, copied into the sg2002 stick bundle. It does not open a framebuffer and it is not in the booted ramdisk or in imageExtraPackagesArm64Nox
later_wayland_in_the_pin.other_session: pd-wayland-session starts /bin/neuswc and Terminal.app. That is the image-wayland / neuswc path, not the M1 ramdisk and not Chonkstep
later_wayland_in_the_pin.m1_panel_scanout: not established. IOGOPFramebuffer being a KC member does not mean it drives this panel

chonkstep.registry_role: Desktop source; Linux-only Wayland backend needs port
evidence: crates/wm-wayland/src/lib.rs is #![cfg(target_os = "linux")] and is empty on any other host
crates/chonkstep-wayland/src/main.rs exits 1 off Linux with the text that it only runs on Linux
crates/wm-wayland/Cargo.toml and crates/chonkstep-wayland/Cargo.toml put their compositor dependencies under cfg(target_os = "linux")
chonkstep.not_the_next_shell: No Chonkstep backend in this workspace can present a Darwin framebuffer. Do not substitute its Linux compositor for the M1 panel.

conclusion: The genuine visible shell is the current /bin/zsh on /dev/console. Current helper source asks the kernel video console to paint that tty (display=2 and serial_video_mirror=1) while serial=3 stays. This review did not boot that helper and did not see the panel. Scanout onto the 13-inch panel remains Claude's. No ramdisk program change paints the panel. Wayland sway/foot and Chonkstep are later sources; neither is a proven M1 display path.
